headline: Am I being lied to?
note:
🔄 REWRITTEN 2026-08-19 to the Natural Tarot-Cut framework. Bubbles 3-6 run as ONE causal chain — so / and / but / that's why — and the read ANSWERS. The art line and the bridge are unchanged. Every ban in this note still stands.

Face-down only (return-mhf). 🔴 NO VERDICT IN EITHER DIRECTION. These three name an untruth outright, so both answers are live harms: 'he lied to you' is an accusation against a real man on no evidence, and 'he is telling you the truth' is a reassurance the funnel has no standing to give — and on this audience the second is the more dangerous of the two. 🔴 Never blame her judgment: naive, gullible, too trusting, 'should have known' are all out. 🔴 No timeframe.

Finding, kept distinct from cards-truth: she has already checked her own read three times, and the checking is the tell. What can be affirmed is the instrument — not the finding it reached.

a: You turned the Magician, dear. Look — his belt sits low and dark against the red robe.
You asked if you're being lied to. Your hand went to the man with a practised hand.
So no honest reader can settle this for you, dear. I won't pretend.
And a hand that practised is hard to read from outside, dear.
But you've gone over this again and again, dear. Something snagged.
That's why you return to it, dear. Your ear caught on something.
Let me look closer at what your ear keeps catching on…
b: You turned the Hanged Man, dear. Look — his knees are bent and one is behind the other.
You asked if you're being lied to. Your hand went to the card that holds a thing open.
So the question won't resolve, dear. Not from where you stand.
And half the shape is behind the other half, dear.
But you can't see round it, dear, and neither can I.
That's why the choice sits wrong, dear. You've had half a picture.
Let me look closer at what has been hiding the other half…
c: You turned the Fool, dear. Look — his sleeve ends in a wide pale cuff.
You asked if you're being lied to. Your hand went to the one with nothing up his sleeve.
So you wanted someone with nothing up the sleeve, dear.
And he's open, dear. Plain, and carrying no trick at all.
But that's exactly what's been missing, dear. I think you know it.
That's why wanting it plain feels like blame, dear. It isn't blame.
Let me look closer at what sits between you and plain dealing…
